items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI atau GTA 6 dikabarkan berjalan pada 30 frame per second (FPS) di konsol, termasuk PlayStation 5 (PS5) dan PS5 Pro. Meski begitu, konfigurasi performa saat gamer resmi dirilis secara global pada 19 November 2026 masih belum dipastikan.
Informasi ini diungkap oleh kreator asal Brasil, Davy Jones, setelah berkunjung ke Rockstar North dan berbicara langsung dengan Rob Nelson, Head of Development sekaligus Co-Director Rockstar North.
Mengutip laporan Flow Games, Jumat (28/8/2026), build GTA 6 yang diperlihatkan dalam kunjungan tersebut berjalan pada 30 FPS di konsol. Flow Games menyebut, kondisi ini berlalu untuk semua konsol, setidaknya ketika dalam tahap pengembangan.
Baca Juga: Bocoran GTA 6 Semakin Masif, Rockstar Games Buka Suara
Davy kemudian menanyakan kemungkinan game penerus GTA 5 ini berjalan pada 60 FPS, termasuk bagaimana performanya di PlayStation 5 Pro.
Nelson belum memberikan jawaban pasti. Ia mengatakan perlu konsultasi lebih lanjut dengan tim teknis Rockstar sebelum memberikan penjelasan lebih detail mengenai konfigurasi performa game ini.
GTA 6 30 FPS Saat Rilis?
Fisik mobil yang lebih realistik ketika meledak di GTA 6 (Sumber: Rockstar Games/Netflix)
Flow Games menjelaskan, pada tahap pengembangan GTA VI saat ini, game tersebut masih berjalan pada 30 FPS di konsol. Laporan sama menekankan kondisi tersebut berlaku “untuk sekarang”, sehingga belum bisa dianggap sebagai konfirmasi versi final GTA 6 nantinya hanya akan menyediakan mode 30 FPS.
Push Square juga melaporkan, game ini menargetkan rilis pada 30 FPS di seluruh konsol berdasarkan informasi Davy Jones dari Rob Nelson. Namun, kemungkinan peningkatan performa masih terbuka karena konfigurasi teknis final belum dipastikan.
Perbedaan ini penting. Target performa selama pengembangan belum tentu identik dengan pilihan mode grafis yang akan tersedia ketika sebuah game dirilis.
Rockstar Games sendiri sampai saat ini belum mengumumkan secara resmi spesifikasi teknis final GTA VI, termasuk pilihan antara Quality Mode dan Performance Mode.
Apakah GTA 6 Akan Punya Mode 60 FPS?
Untuk saat ini, jawabannya belum diketahui. Rockstar Games maupun Rockstar North masih bungkam terkait Performance Mode 60 FPS untuk GTA 6. Nelson juga belum memastikan apakah opsi tersebut dapat tersedia ketika game diluncurkan atau ditambahkan setelah dirilis.
Detail teknis lain seperti resolusi rendering dan penggunaan ray tracing juga belum dijelaskan secara resmi. Hal yang sama berlaku untuk PS5 Pro. Belum ada informasi resmi mengenai apakah konsol tersebut akan mendapatkan mode grafis atau performa khusus untuk GTA 6.
Karena itu, terlalu dini menyimpulkan PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, maupun Xbox Series S akan terkunci pada konfigurasi performa yang sama ketika versi final tersedia.
Gameplay GTA 6 Extended Look Direkam di PS5
Ada satu informasi mengenai performa konsol yang sudah dikonfirmasi langsung oleh Rockstar Games. Video Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look yang dirilis 27 Agustus 2026 direkam sepenuhnya menggunakan footage in-game dari PlayStation 5.
Rockstar menyebut video tersebut sebagai tampilan lebih jauh terhadap dunia dan gameplay GTA 6.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pak Datacom Limited has come under scrutiny over a Rs 556.8 million solar-panel transaction, with a detailed complaint seeking an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) into the company’s procurement, payment, internal-audit, and corporate-governance processes.
The allegations are contained in a 23-page complaint and accompanying internal records linked to former Pak Datacom chief executive Brigadier (retd) Syed Zulfiqar Ali, who headed the company for nearly five years.
Complaint document
According to the complaint, Pak Datacom paid Rs 556.828 million on May 25, 2026, to Karachi-based company MSBI as an advance for the purchase of solar panels. The same stock was later reported to have been sold to another Karachi-based company, Fabrica, with invoices issued in June.
Around Rs 556 million was expected to be recovered from Fabrica by August 31, 2026, according to the documents cited in the complaint.
The complaint questions whether normal procurement, commercial, internal-audit, and computerized recording procedures were fully followed during the transaction. It also raises concerns over the physical movement of the solar panels, approval mechanisms and the role of different departments within the company.
Pak Datacom officials, however, have rejected the allegations.
Ali Saleem Rana and General Manager Waseem Ahmed said the claims were being made by the company’s former chief executive and had no basis in fact. They maintained that major business and financial decisions at Pak Datacom are taken with the approval of the board of directors and in accordance with established company procedures.
Procurement, Delivery and Audit Processes Questioned
The complaint alleges that the transaction involved around 20 to 30 containers of solar panels and claims that parts of the deal may have been processed largely through documentation rather than the normal commercial workflow.
It further raises questions over whether gate passes and movement documents corresponded with the actual physical delivery of the goods.
However, the material provided does not conclusively establish that the goods were not delivered, and no independent regulatory finding on the allegation has been cited.
The complaint also questions the relationship between MSBI, which sold the solar panels, and Fabrica, which purchased them from Pak Datacom. It alleges that the two companies may have had a common underlying interest.
The accompanying documents, however, do not include SECP records establishing common ownership between the two entities.
Another major concern raised in the complaint is that Pak Datacom’s commercial and solar-business teams were allegedly not fully involved in the transaction.
It claims that senior officials including the chief commercial officer, general manager south, deputy general manager solar business, senior marketing manager and relevant account managers were either unaware of or excluded from important parts of the deal.
The complaint further alleges that the transaction was not subjected to a pre-audit despite an existing board-approved policy and was not fully processed through the company’s Odoo computerized system.
Pak Datacom management disputes these assertions and says the relevant business and financial decisions were undertaken with board approval and that the company possesses supporting legal and commercial records.
SECP Asked to Examine Governance and Financial Questions
The documents show that Pak Datacom had entered the solar business well before the disputed 2026 transaction.
The company’s solar expansion plans were discussed at the board’s 214th meeting in October 2022, when approval was given to import up to 48 containers annually.
By August 2023, Pak Datacom had begun importing solar panels directly from Chinese manufacturer LONGi. An April 2025 business plan stated that the company had imported and sold 25 containers, equivalent to about 10.7MW of solar panels, generating reported revenue of around Rs 364 million.
The complaint argues that the earlier direct-import model was more profitable than the 2026 transaction conducted through a local supplier.
It estimates that if around Rs 500 million had remained invested with a commercial bank for approximately three months, it could have generated returns of between Rs 12.5 million and Rs 15 million, compared with an estimated net profit of around Rs 10.5 million from the solar deal after taxes and other costs.
These calculations are part of the complainant’s assessment and have not been independently verified.
The complaint also links the transaction to Pak Datacom’s financial performance, citing a decline in earnings per share and revenue during the nine months ended April 2026.
On that basis, it alleges that booking a solar sale of more than Rs 500 million before the close of the financial year may have significantly increased reported revenue.
Beyond the solar transaction, the complaint raises questions over other company expenditures between July 2025 and June 2026, including alleged spending on vehicles, board meetings and committee-related payments.
It asks the SECP to examine whether competitive bids were sought, whether the procurement committee and full board formally approved the deal, whether any disclosure obligations arose for the Pakistan Stock Exchange and shareholders, and whether the transaction was consistent with the company’s constitutional documents.
The complainant has also sought an examination of broader allegations concerning possible misuse of funds, commissions and other financial benefits.
However, the documents cited do not provide conclusive evidence establishing money laundering, illicit commissions or diversion of funds, and no regulatory finding has been made on those claims.
Pak Datacom officials have maintained that the allegations are unfounded and that all major commercial and financial decisions were taken under board oversight and in line with established rules.
The matter now rests with the SECP, which has been asked to examine the transaction, the role of management, and the responsibilities of the board under the Companies Act, 2017 and relevant corporate-governance provisions.

items.content:
Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, smartphone flagship HUAWEI selalu mencoba hadir secara konsisten memberikan pengalaman fotografi mobile tingkat lanjut, mendorong batas inovasi yang ada dari tahun ke tahun. Kehadiran HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G di Indonesia juga hadir sebagai versi terbaru dari pengembangan teknologi kamera hingga pemrosesan gambar berbasis AI terbaru dari HUAWEI, agar mampu menjawab tantangan yang kerap dialami ketika menangkap momen menggunakan smartphone.
HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G siap memungkinkan pengguna untuk dapat menangkap momen sedekat mungkin dengan apa yang mereka lihat dan rasakan, lewat penggabungan sejumlah teknologi terbaru. Mulai dari 200MP Ultra Large Sensor Telephoto Camera, sensor True-to-Colour Camera 2.0 yang eksklusif hadir di smartphone HUAWEI, hingga Advanced AI Photography Experience, semua dihadirkan lewat sebuah smartphone yang tampil premium. Memungkinkan penangkapan momen dengan detail, serta warna dan perspektif yang sebelumnya lebih sulit diwujudkan.
Lebih dari sekadar spesifikasi di atas kertas, HUAWEI mencoba untuk memberikan standar baru yang sesungguhnya di tengah persaingan smartphone flagship yang semakin sengit. Lantas bagaimana HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G bisa memberikan pengalaman memuaskan baik saat digunakan untuk menangkap momen paling spesial, hingga mendukung aktivitas harian?
Sistem Kamera Superior Untuk Sudut Pandang Lebih Beragam
Dinamakan HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G, tersedia dua pilihan flagship yang dapat Gizmo friends pilih sesuai dengan kebutuhan. Meski begitu, masing-masing tetap hadir membawa inovasi kamera paling mutakhir dari HUAWEI. Dan pada HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G, dihadirkan sebuah terobosan baru melalui setup 200MP Ultra Large Sensor Telephoto Camera.
Ya, sensor telefoto smartphone ini membawa dimensi sensor 1/1,28 inci, notabene merupakan dimensi yang umumnya disematkan sebagai sensor utama. Dengan begitu, lebih banyak detail dan cahaya yang bisa ditangkap, terutama ketika dipasangkan dengan teknologi RYYB, diafragma f/2.6, serta stabilisasi tingkat hardware alias OIS.
Membawa 4x Optical Zoom, sensor telefoto HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G juga mendukung fitur Telephoto Macro, alias mampu menangkap objek terkecil secara dekat dalam detail terbaik, untuk eksplorasi detail dari berbagai jarak. Tak hanya unggul pada sektor fotografi, sensor ini juga membawa kemampuan Industry-Leading 20x HEX Telephoto Video. Alias bisa memberikan pembesaran lebih jauh pada videografi, dalam kualitas yang tetap terjaga.
Menggunakan 1x zoom
Menggunakan 10x zoom
20x zoom masih bisa memberikan detail yang baik
Tidak hanya sensor telefotonya saja yang dirancang spesial, HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G juga membawa Ultra Lighting HDR Camera 50MP dengan sensor besar 1/1,28 inci berjenis RYYB, 10 tingkat adjustable physical aperture f/1.4-f/4.0, OIS, plus teknologi LOFIC—memungkinkan penangkapan rentang dinamis yang lebih luas, termasuk untuk kebutuhan penangkapan gambar maupun perekaman video dalam skenario pencahayaan lebih kompleks seperti backlight maupun low-light.
Kamera HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max mampu menangkap warna yang kaya sekaligus akurat dalam kondisi low-light
Sensor telefoto superior membantu menangkap detail terkecil dalam sebuah makanan dalam ketajaman tinggi
Tidak hanya varian Pro Max, HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro 5G juga membawa Ultra Lighting Macro Telephoto Camera 50MP berjenis RYYB dengan 4x Optical Zoom, 8X Optical-Quality Zoom, diafragma f/2.1, serta OIS. Sesuai namanya, sensor ini membawa kemampuan fokus jarak dekat hingga 5cm, untuk menangkap detail objek seperti tekstur makanan, perhiasan, hingga lainnya yang mungkin sulit untuk ditangkap dari jarak normal.
Tidak hanya sensor telefoto unggul, HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro 5G juga membawa Ultra Lighting Main Camera 50MP dengan sensor besar 1/1,28 inci, teknologi RYYB, OIS, dan juga 10 tingkat adjustable physical aperture f/1.4-f/4.0. Kedua varian HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G juga didukung True-to-Color Camera 2.0 yang mampu membantu hasilkan reproduksi warna lebih akurat sekaligus natural.
Kombinasi sensor yang superior membuat kamera HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G mampu menangkap gambar hingga merekam video dari berbagai jarak dalam kualitas terbaik, memberikan pengalaman flagship dengan fleksibilitas tinggi. Mulai dari detail tekstur makanan, warna langit maupun pemandangan indah, sampai warna kulit, semua dapat ditangkap dalam kualitas dan visual yang lebih nyata, alias mendekati apa yang terlihat oleh pandangan mata.
Diperkuat Fitur Advanced AI Untuk Sempurnakan Setiap Momen
Selain mengandalkan kombinasi hardware yang inovatif, HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G juga diperkuat serangkaian fitur AI yang mampu membantu menangkap momen terbaik, tidak hanya setelah gambar ditangkap, namun juga dalam proses penangkapannya. Beberapa di antaranya termasuk AI Remove yang bisa menghapus objek mengganggu dalam gambar, AI Best Expression untuk mengubah ekspresi wajah menjadi yang terbaik dalam sebuah foto grup, hingga AI De-glare untuk membantu mengurangi efek pantulan agar objek terlihat lebih jelas.
Namun selain ketiga fitur AI tersebut, HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G juga membawa fitur eksklusif bernama AI Composition. Ya, sesuai namanya, pengguna akan mendapatkan panduan komposisi pengambilan gambar secara real-time, demi framing optimal. Tidak hanya angle, juga rentang zoom yang pas sesuai dengan skenario yang terdeteksi oleh kamera. Setelah gambar tertangkap, ada AI Move yang memungkinkan objek pada gambar dipindahkan tata letaknya, untuk komposisi lebih kreatif.
Petal Interconnect Mempermudah File Sharing, Tampil dalam Opsi Warna Segar
Untuk membagikan momen yang berhasil ditangkap dalam kualitas tinggi, kedua smartphone kini mengusung Petal Interconnect. Sebuah fitur yang memudahkan pengiriman file antar perangkat HUAWEI dengan iOS, sebagai opsi kirim data yang jauh lebih seamless. HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G juga hadir membawa dukungan hingga 100W Wired HUAWEI SuperCharge dan 80W Wireless HUAWEI SuperCharge untuk varian Pro Max, lengkap dengan perlindungan Anti-Reflection and Scratch-Resistant Kunlun Glass serta sertifikasi IP68 dan IP69 yang membuatnya tahan debu serta air.
HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G hadir dalam opsi warna Orange Ocean, Blush Gold, serta Graphite Black. Sementara HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro yang membawa dukungan 66W Wired dan 50W Wireless SuperCharge, tersedia dalam warna Guava Soda, Orange Soda, Coconut White, dan Mulberry Black. Dan tentunya, pengguna dapat mengakses kebutuhan digital harian secara komplit lewat HUAWEI AppGallery.
Aplikasi Tersedia Komplit di HUAWEI AppGallery
Ketersediaan atau ekosistem aplikasi tentu menjadi penting, sebagai pelengkap pengalaman menggunakan smartphone flagship. Dan melalui HUAWEI AppGallery, pengguna HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G bisa mendapatkan semua aplikasi yang dibutuhkan untuk aktivitas termasuk produktivitas harian. Mulai dari perbankan, hiburan, hingga kreasi konten.
Aplikasi harian seperti WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Spotify, hingga Netflix tentu tersedia. Bagaimana dengan e-commerce maupun super app? Juga tersedia, mulai Gojek, Grab, Shopee, dan Tokopedia. Konten kreator juga bisa mendapatkan CapCut hingga Canva dan Lightroom, sementara aplikasi perbankan seperti BCA mobile, Livin’ by Mandiri, BRImo, BNI Mobile Banking, hingga e-wallet seperti DANA, GoPay, OVO, hingga ShopeePay juga bisa didapatkan. 
Bahkan untuk Gizmo friends yang sudah menggunakan platform AI dalam keseharian, juga bisa mengakses Gemini, DeepSeek, hingga Dola secara lancar. Sistem keamanan 360° Protection HUAWEI AppGallery juga hadir memastikan bila semua aplikasi di dalamnya terjamin aman, karena harus melalui sejumlah proses khusus seperti verifikasi pengembang, pemindaian malware, perlindungan privasi, hingga pemeriksaan integritas aplikasi. 
HUAWEI Pura 90s Series 5G Sudah Bisa Dipesan, Bonus Hingga Rp8,4 Juta
Tertarik untuk membeli flagship HUAWEI terbaru? HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G 12GB + 512GB dibanderol Rp22.999 juta, sementara HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro 5G 12GB + 512GB dipasarkan dengan harga Rp17.999 juta.
Pada September mendatang, HUAWEI juga akan menghadirkan varian dengan kapasitas penyimpanan 256GB, yakni HUAWEI Pura 90s Pro Max 5G 12GB + 256GB dengan harga Rp20.999 juta dan HUAWEI Pura 90 Pro 5G 12GB + 256GB seharga Rp15.999 juta.
Bonus tersebut terdiri dari Free 2x Memory Upgrade senilai Rp2 juta, HUAWEI Watch Fit 4 senilai Rp1,8 juta, Bank Cashback senilai hingga Rp2 juta, serta proteksi HUAWEI Care senilai Rp2,6 juta. Proteksi tersebut mencakup kerusakan yang tidak disengaja selama 1 tahun, serta layanan penggantian screen protector hingga 4 kali selama 2 tahun.
HUAWEI juga memberikan opsi pembiayaan lewat Home Credit dengan bunga 0%, bebas biaya administrasi, serta bebas DP. Dan untuk melengkapi peluncuran HUAWEI Pura 90s Series di Indonesia, HUAWEI berkolaborasi dengan AMAN, menghadirkan pengalaman premium bagi para konsumen.
Selama periode hingga 31 Oktober 2026, konsumen yang memenuhi syarat, bisa menikmati penawaran khusus yakni exclusive stay offer hingga 40% di sejumlah property AMAN di Indonesia. HUAWEI Pura 90s Series tersedia secara daring di HUAWEI Store, Shopee, Lazada, Tokopedia, TikTok Shop, Blibli, erafone.com, dan Eraspace. Dan tentunya juga bisa dipesan secara luring melalui jaringan HUAWEI Authorized Experience Store, Erafone, Blibli, Urban Republic, Digiplus, serta peritel resmi HUAWEI lainnya.

The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication is preparing to introduce a fresh Pakistan Telecommunications (Reorganization) Amendment Bill, 2026, after deciding to withdraw the existing legislation from the Senate in an effort to avoid further procedural delays.
In a statement issued on August 28, the ministry said the current bill was nearing the end of its 90-day constitutional period in the Senate.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication is preparing to introduce a fresh Pakistan Telecommunications (Reorganization) Amendment Bill, 2026, after deciding to withdraw the existing legislation from the Senate in an effort to avoid further procedural delays.
In a statement issued on August 28, the ministry said the current bill was nearing the end of its 90-day constitutional period in the Senate.
Once that period expired, the legislation would have moved to a joint sitting of Parliament, which the ministry said might not be convened in the near future.
To prevent the process from slowing further, MoITT said it had chosen to withdraw the current bill and introduce a fresh version through the regular legislative route.
The ministry said the new bill would retain the core substance and policy intent of the proposed legislation while allowing the process to move forward in a more timely and effective manner.
The development comes after the earlier telecom amendment bill faced criticism and prolonged scrutiny in the Senate, particularly over provisions linked to right-of-way, telecom infrastructure deployment and access to private property.
Lawmakers had raised concerns over how some of the proposed provisions could affect property rights and the process through which telecom operators gain access for fiber, towers, and other infrastructure.
The government’s latest move indicates that it is not abandoning the broader telecom reform agenda. Instead, it is seeking a faster legislative route by restarting the process with a new bill.
The fresh draft could also give the ministry an opportunity to refine contested provisions while preserving the broader objective of creating a more streamlined framework for telecom infrastructure and right-of-way issues.
Pakistan’s telecom sector has long cited inconsistent approval processes, infrastructure permissions, and right-of-way disputes as major barriers to faster fibre and network expansion.
With the previous bill now being withdrawn, attention will shift to the timing and contents of the fresh legislation, which MOITT is expected to bring before Parliament as the next step in its telecom reform agenda.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian agri-tech startup UfarmX, which leverages blockchain technology to empower rural, unbanked and underserved smallholder farmers, has facilitated over US$6.8 million in agricultural commerce across Nigeria, Senegal, and Liberia, with further expansion into Kenya planned.
The UfarmX platform does various different things, connecting farmers to quality inputs, much of it on credit utilising a transparent blockchain ledger; allowing them access to markets post-harvest; and giving them the data they need to scale their operations.
Disrupt Africa reported in 2023 the startup had expanded to Senegal, and it is now also active in Liberia. Across those three markets, where Ufarmx works with over 17,000 credit-scored farmers and a growing network of vetted retail partners, it has facilitated over US$6.8 million in agricultural commerce.
Its insured retailer channel is running a net default rate of 1.17 per cent, collateral-free, in a sector the continent’s banks price as untouchable. Alexander Zanders, CEO of UfarmX, told Disrupt Africa the startup had launched with direct lending to prove the model.
“Farmers repaid, yields improved, revenues grew. But banks move too slowly to build a company around. So we built the retail model instead – local retailers extend credit to farmers using our data, without needing a bank in the loop at all,” he said.
This is simply phase one for UfarmX, with phase two arriving at the end of this year – a credit-scoring API that lets banks and financial institutions process agricultural loan applications directly on UfarmX’s underwriting, the way American lenders run decisions on Equifax or Experian.
An expansion into Kenya, the company’s first East African market, is also planned for Q4. Ahead of the API launch, UfarmX is opening conversations with banks, DFIs, insurers, and input producers that want early access to the underwriting rail.
“African agriculture gets looked at through the lens of impact, when the opportunity for capitalisation is immense. This isn’t charity. It’s the largest credit market still sitting untouched,” said Zanders.

items.author: Kavit Majithia
items.content:
INTERVIEW: The director general of the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) argued the country is better placed than some global rivals to become a 6G leader, but conceded there could be some “slippages” on the road to a commercial launch in 2030.
Speaking on the Mobile World Live Podcast, S.P Kochhar (pictured) reiterated the government’s ambitions for India to take a leading role in developing the technology, insisting this “is not just a statement” and active steps are being taken to make it happen.
He pointed to concrete examples including a drive to ensure at least 10% of global 6G patents come from India, the formation of relevant committees and forums, and investment in fabrication plants to ensure silicon is being made in the country.
This last point, he believes, is giving India a competitive advantage.
“Because of the cost differential with the western world, we should be in a better position, better placed, to provide 6G compared to others.”
He also pointed out some countries may be able to manufacture cheaper or on par, but “the trust factor is also in favour of India”.
With a push to integrate AI across the entire process and development of quantum, Kochhar argues “it is a very well-planned roadmap which has been enunciated and put into practice”.
He continued: “This time around, it is not a policy which will remain in the cupboard.”
Eyebrows
Kochhar dismissed any notions that India was late to the party when it came to 5G, stating it is not the nation’s responsibility “to reinvent zero”. It is, in fact, using the mistakes from others in the 5G era to avoid the same problems with 6G.
“If we can learn from others’ mistakes, why should I commit a mistake?” he asked.
While Kochhar subscribes to the government’s bullishness around 6G, he did admit there could be some bumps in the road, particularly in keeping pace with a widely-expected launch for the technology in 2030.
“I see some slippages there because 5G monetisation has not taken place the way it should,” he said. “Putting in more money in 6G at this point in time may raise eyebrows and that might delay the programme for some time. But that is my personal view.”

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The government has moved ahead with the establishment of a sovereign, cloud-based and AI-enabled data centre of the National Telecommunication Corporation (NTC) in Karachi, with the project already entering the procurement phase.
Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunications Shaza Fatima Khawaja, in a written reply to the National Assembly, said the “Establishment of NTC Data Center at Karachi” project was approved under the Annual Development Programme (ADP) 2025-26 and is currently under procurement.
The minister said the facility has been designed primarily to cater to the market of NTC’s South Region, including government entities operating in the region. The initial setup is being procured at present and would subsequently be scaled up according to the requirements of government clients.
According to NTC, the project is aimed at establishing sovereign data centre infrastructure within Pakistan, reducing dependence on foreign cloud platforms while providing basic AI services and strengthening data sovereignty, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance and operational resilience.
The facility is expected to address the growing computing and storage requirements of the NTC South Region and provide localized hosting services to federal and provincial government entities operating across Sindh and Balochistan.
NTC said the data centre would offer Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS), Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), disaster recovery and business continuity services. The regional facility is expected to reduce pressure on infrastructure nodes in northern parts of the country while improving the reliability, availability and response times of critical e-governance platforms.
The government also expects the Karachi facility to reinforce implementation of the Pakistan Cloud First Policy by providing a standardized and secure domestic cloud framework for government organizations.
NTC said keeping public-sector data within Pakistan’s geographical boundaries would help shield government data from foreign supply-chain risks, international pricing fluctuations and geopolitical vulnerabilities.
In a significant step towards establishing NTC as a trusted sovereign cloud provider, seven applications have been submitted for accreditation under the Pakistan Cloud First Policy, including NTC itself, the reply added.
The Karachi data centre will also incorporate foundational AI capabilities in line with Pakistan’s emerging National AI Policy framework.
According to NTC, its regional AI-capable node would operate through a vendor-neutral computing stack and sovereign, locally contextualized large language models (LLMs), enabling secure AI inference and model deployment for strategic public-sector applications.
The facility is also expected to give a push to the domestic IT sector by enabling government institutions to shift from expensive foreign cloud platforms to locally hosted infrastructure, potentially reducing operational costs and conserving foreign exchange.
NTC said the scalable architecture of the data centre would allow capacity to be expanded in line with market demand, creating infrastructure for the growth of e-governance, digital public services and technology-driven innovation in sectors including health, education, finance and industry.
The project, therefore, is being positioned not merely as a regional data centre but as a key component of Pakistan’s efforts to build sovereign digital infrastructure, strengthen control over government data and support the country’s transition towards cloud and AI-enabled public services.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Universal Service Fund (USF) has provided voice and broadband access to more than 16.2 million people living in 9,400-plus underserved and unserved mauzas during the last five fiscal years, while deploying over 10,400 kilometres of optic fibre cable (OFC) and connecting 947 unserved areas.
According to a written reply submitted by Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja to the National Assembly, USF projects have significantly expanded digital connectivity in rural and remote areas where commercial deployment by telecom operators was not considered viable.
The ministry said USF interventions had enabled broadband services for the first time in several target areas and helped bridge the communication gap in unserved and underserved communities.
During FY2022-26, USF access projects provided voice and broadband data services to 16.2 million-plus people residing in more than 9,400 mauzas.
The fund also provided broadband coverage along more than 1,000 kilometres of previously unserved road segments on national highways and motorways, besides covering eight tourist destinations and around 50 kilometres of access routes.
Under its optic-fibre backhaul programme, USF deployed 10,400-plus kilometres of OFC during the last five fiscal years, connecting 947 unserved tehsil headquarters, union councils and towns.
The government said USF had been established under Section 33(A)(1) of the Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996, with the mandate to extend telecommunications services to unserved, underserved, rural and remote communities.
USF has implemented projects under two broad categories—access projects and backhaul projects.
Access projects have evolved from providing voice and basic data services through 2G networks in unserved mauzas to high-speed broadband services through 3G and 4G networks. The programme has also been extended to unserved road segments and tourist locations.
Since inception, USF has provided voice and broadband data services to more than 38.4 million people across 22,100-plus mauzas, according to the ministry.
It has also provided broadband coverage to more than 2,500 kilometres of unserved road segments on national highways and motorways, along with eight tourist destinations and approximately 50 kilometres of access routes.
Under the OFC programme, USF has deployed more than 18,300 kilometres of optic fibre since inception and connected 1,089 unserved tehsil headquarters, union councils and towns.
The ministry said the OFC projects had evolved from connecting unserved tehsil headquarters and towns to extending connectivity to union councils and other areas with access-network infrastructure, thereby expanding the overall fibre footprint in unserved and underserved regions.
According to the government, improved connectivity in remote areas was generating socio-economic benefits by expanding access to education, healthcare, emergency services, financial inclusion, e-governance and economic opportunities.
The ministry maintained that USF projects had produced significant improvements in connectivity, particularly in areas where telecom operators had little commercial incentive to deploy infrastructure.
It said USF would continue identifying and serving unserved and underserved areas across the country through broadband access and fibre-optic infrastructure projects.

items.title: Directions under Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – The Citizens Co-operative Bank Ltd., Jammu
items.summary: It is hereby notified for information of the public that in exercise of powers vested in it under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) vide Directive Ref. No. पर्य.वि.जम्मू. सं.S132/12-01-040/2026-27 dated August 25, 2026 has issued certain Directions to The Citizens Co-operative Bank Ltd., Jammu, (“the bank”), whereby, as from the close of business on August 27, 2026, the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as notified in
items.content:
It is hereby notified for information of the public that in exercise of powers vested in it under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) vide Directive Ref. No. पर्य.वि.जम्मू. सं.S132/12-01-040/2026-27 dated August 25, 2026 has issued certain Directions to The Citizens Co-operative Bank Ltd., Jammu, (“the bank”), whereby, as from the close of business on August 27, 2026, the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as notified in the RBI Direction dated August 25, 2026, a copy of which has been directed to be displayed on the bank's website / premises for perusal by interested members of the public. Considering the bank's present liquidity position, the bank has been directed to allow withdrawal of ₹1,25,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Five Thousand only) from savings bank or current accounts or any other account of a depositor but is allowed to set off loans against deposits subject to the conditions stated in the above RBI Directions. The bank may incur expenditure in respect of certain essential items such as salaries of employees, rent, electricity bills, etc., as specified in the said Directions.
2. RBI has in the recent past engaged with the Board and Senior Management of the bank for improvement in its functioning. However, lack of concrete efforts taken by the bank to address the supervisory concerns and to protect the interest of depositors of the bank, necessitated issuance of these Directions.
3. The eligible depositors would be entitled to receive deposit insurance claim amount of their deposits upto a monetary ceiling of ₹5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakh only) in the same capacity and in the same right, from the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), as applicable under the provisions of the DICGC Act, 1961, based on submission of willingness by the depositors concerned and after due verification. The depositors may contact the bank officials for further information. Details may also be accessed on the DICGC website: www.dicgc.org.in.
4. The issue of the above Directions by the RBI should not per se be construed as cancellation of the banking license by RBI. The bank will continue to undertake banking business subject to restrictions specified in the said Directions till its financial position improves. The RBI continues to monitor the position of the bank and will take necessary actions including modifications of these Directions, as warranted, depending upon circumstances and in the interest of the depositors.
5. These Directions shall remain in force for a period of six months from the close of business on August 27, 2026 and are subject to review.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/978

items.content:
Today, the Reserve Bank released the data on performance of the private corporate business sector during the first quarter of 2026-27, drawn from abridged quarterly financial results of 3,247 listed non-government non-financial companies1. This summary position also includes comparable data for Q4:2025-26 and Q1:2025-26 to enable study of sequential (q-o-q) and annual (y-o-y) change (web-link:
https://data.rbi.org.in/DBIE/#/dbie/reports/Statistics/Corporate%20Sector/Listed%20Non-Government%20Non-Financial%20Companies).
Highlights
Sales
At aggregate level, sales growth of listed private non-financial companies continued to accelerate to 19.4 per cent (y-o-y) during Q1:2026-27 from 13.9 per cent in the previous quarter (Table 1A and 2A).
Sales of 1,827 listed private manufacturing companies expanded by 21.4 per cent (y-o-y) during Q1:2026-27, up from 14.5 per cent in the previous quarter. This acceleration was majorly driven by the automobiles, petroleum and electrical machinery industries (Table 1A, 2A and 5A).
Sales growth of Information Technology (IT) companies strengthened further and recorded a double-digit growth of 14.8 per cent (y-o-y) during Q1:2026-27 from 9.9 per cent in the previous quarter.
Non-IT services companies continued to record a healthy double-digit growth of 19.7 per cent (20.3 per cent in the previous quarter), mainly driven by wholesale and retail trade industry.
Expenditure
With global supply chain disruptions, raw material expenses of manufacturing companies rose substantially by 27.5 per cent (y-o-y) during Q1:2026-27; however, raw material to sales ratio declined marginally to 58.1 per cent during Q1 from 58.5 per cent in the previous quarter (Table 2A and 2B).
Staff cost of manufacturing, IT and non-IT services companies rose by 12.4 per cent, 7.6 per cent and 11.2 per cent, respectively, during Q1:2026-27, higher than the growth recorded during the previous quarter. Staff cost to sales ratio for manufacturing and non-IT services companies increased to 5.5 per cent and 10.1 per cent, respectively, in Q1:2026-27; however, it declined for IT companies during Q1 from the previous quarter.
Pricing power
Despite significant increase in input costs, operating profit growth of manufacturing companies improved significantly to 21.3 per cent (y-o-y) during Q1:2026-27 from 9.4 per cent in the previous quarter. Operating profit growth of IT and non-IT services companies also improved to 19.9 per cent and 12.7 per cent, respectively, during Q1:2026-27 (Table 2A).
On sequential basis, operating profit margin improved across all major sectors during Q1:2026-27 (Chart 2 and Table 2B).
Interest expenses
With higher sequential rise in gross profits than interest expense, manufacturing companies’ interest coverage ratio (ICR)2 improved to 10.2 in Q1:2026-27. ICR of non-IT services companies increased to 2.6 and ICR of IT firms continued to remain at elevated level during Q1 (Table 2B).
List of Tables

B Select Ratios
2 A Performance of Listed Non-Government Non-Financial Companies – Sector-wise Growth Rates
B Select Ratios
3 A Performance of Listed Non-Government Non-Financial Companies according to Size of Paid-up-Capital Growth Rates
B Select Ratios
4 A Performance of Listed Non-Government Non-Financial Companies according to Size of Sales Growth Rates
B Select Ratios
5 A Performance of Listed Non-Government Non-Financial Companies according to Industry Growth Rates
B Select Ratios
Explanatory Notes
Glossary
Notes:
The coverage of companies in different quarters varies, depending on the date of declaration of results; this is, however, not expected to significantly alter the aggregate position.
Explanatory notes detailing the compilation methodology, and the glossary (including revised definitions and calculations that differ from previous releases) are appended.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/974
1 Source: Capitaline database
2 ICR (i.e., ratio of earnings before interest and tax to interest expenses) is a measure of debt servicing capacity of a company. The minimum value for ICR is 1 for a company to be viable.

items.title: Govt Announces Rs. 5 Million Compensation for Each Family Affected by PIMS Fire
items.summary:
The government has announced financial compensation of Rs5 million for the families of each newborn who died in the PIMS Hospital fire incident.
According to the announcement, the federal government stands with the affected families in their grief and sorrow. It said no amount of financial compensation can replace precious human lives.
The statement added that the deceased children cannot be brought back, but the assistance is meant to ease the hardships of the grieving families and offer some relief.
The government said it will extend every possible support and assistance to the affected families.
It may be recalled that 14 newborn babies lost their lives in a fire that broke out in the nursery of PIMS Hospital yesterday.

items.author: Olusola Jide Jide
items.content:
The crisis rocking Nigerian football reached a defining moment yesterday as the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) President, Ibrahim Musa Gusau, resigned from office alongside members of his board, bringing an abrupt end to an administration that had come under mounting pressure over the state of the country’s football.
Gusau announced his resignation before members of staff and journalists at the federation’s headquarters in Abuja. The development marked the collapse of a leadership structure elected in October 2022, with promises of stability, development and improved football administration.
The Zamfara-born administrator said his decision followed consultations with relevant stakeholders and his family, adding that his exit was aimed at creating room for reforms within the federation.
“I consulted, I had to inform them, and I decided to resign as president of the NFF. My resignation is intended to give way to a comprehensive and orderly reform process aimed at addressing the longstanding institutional, governance and developmental challenges confronting Nigerian football”. He added: “I have decided to resign my position. I have also advised my board members to resign”.
2027: Hurdles before the coalition
Subsidy or no Subsidy? Tinubu promises cheaper transport from Oct
The statement effectively ended an administration that had previously appeared determined to seek another mandate.
Gusau’s departure was not merely a personal decision. It came after months of turbulence that placed his administration under intense scrutiny.
The NFF leadership had been confronted by a series of setbacks, including Nigeria’s failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the Super Falcons’ historic failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, declining performances from age-grade teams, concerns over financial management, investigations by security and anti-corruption agencies, growing dissatisfaction among football stakeholders, uncertainty over the federation’s electoral process among others.
Major issues that forced Gusau’s exit
Double World Cup mishaps: For the Super Eagles, missing out on the 2026 FIFA World Cup represented another major setback after the team also failed to qualify for the 2022 edition of the tournament.
The back-to-back failures transformed disappointment into a national debate over the direction of Nigerian football.
Super Falcons’ historic failure: The team failed to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup, ending Nigeria’s record of appearing in every edition of the competition since it began in 1991.
The Falcons’ failure was particularly damaging because the team had long been regarded as the most successful women’s football side in Africa and one of Nigeria’s strongest sporting brands.
The two qualification failures shifted criticism from coaches and players to the leadership of the NFF.
Pressure from ex-internationals: Former internationals, football administrators and supporters began demanding answers, questioning whether the federation had the right structures and policies to sustain Nigeria’s football success.
For Gusau and his board, the challenge was no longer only about results on the pitch. It had become a question of confidence in the entire football administration system.
Decline in age-grade football: Beyond the senior national teams, Nigeria’s youth football structures also became a source of concern.
The country’s Under-17 and Under-20 teams had traditionally served as a major pathway for developing players who later represented the senior national teams.
Nigeria’s success at youth tournaments had helped establish the country as one of the world’s leading producers of football talent.
However, declining consistency from the age-grade teams raised concerns about the strength of the development system.
While individual failures can be blamed on factors such as coaching decisions, injuries or poor form, simultaneous struggles across the senior teams and youth structures suggested deeper institutional problems.
That was one of the major criticisms the Gusau administration faced.
Financial scrutiny: The crisis within the federation deepened as questions emerged over the management of government intervention funds meant to address outstanding financial obligations to members of Nigeria’s national teams.
Reports indicated that security and anti-corruption agencies were examining documents relating to the utilisation of the funds.
Different accounts cited figures of N17 billion and N12 billion, although the exact amount involved and the full scope of the investigations require official clarification which Daily Trust was unable to get as at press time.
The Department of State Services (DSS) was reported to have requested documents concerning the funds, while the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) were also linked to wider scrutiny of the federation’s finances.
Committee report fails to calm storm
In response to Nigeria’s poor performances at international competitions, the NFF established a fact-finding committee to investigate the causes of the setbacks and recommend solutions.
The committee, headed by former NFF General Secretary Ambassador, Fanny Amun, was expected to provide a roadmap for addressing the challenges facing Nigerian football.
However, Amun resigned after submitting his report, saying he wanted to protect the integrity and independence of the committee’s work.
Daily Trust gathered that his resignation raised concerns among stakeholders on whether the recommendations would be implemented and whether the federation was prepared to undertake the reforms demanded.
The political situation within the NFF also contributed to the eventual collapse of the Gusau-led administration.
With the federation’s elective congress scheduled for September 27 in Lafia, Nasarawa State, Gusau had been preparing for another term in office.
However, reports emerged that members of the 13-man Executive Committee were considering mass resignation.
Eight members were reportedly ready to leave, with further resignations potentially leading to the collapse of the board.
Gusau’s decision to advise his board members to resign, therefore, has wider implications beyond his own departure.
NSC at the centre of transition talks
The National Sports Commission (NSC) is now central to discussions about the next steps for Nigerian football.
The commission has moved towards a possible restructuring of the NFF, including consideration of a three-month normalisation committee to oversee the federation and prepare the ground for a fresh electoral process.
That were speculations that the federal government had ordered the resignation of Gusau and his board, but the NSC denied the claim.
The resignation of the NFF leadership may have prevented a direct confrontation with FIFA, whose regulations prohibit government interference in the running of national football associations.
A government takeover of the federation could expose Nigeria to possible sanctions, including suspension from FIFA competitions.
Football officials reportedly worked behind the scenes to secure a voluntary resignation process that would create room for reforms without giving the appearance of government interference.
However, Daily Trust gathered that any new arrangement will be closely monitored by FIFA and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).
Gusau’s resignation has created a leadership vacuum but also opened the door for a major restructuring of Nigerian football.
An emergency NFF Congress has been summoned in Abuja to deliberate on the crisis and determine the immediate future of the federation.
Representatives from State Football Associations, clubs, coaches, players and referees are expected to participate.
The Congress will decide how the NFF operates during the transition period and what happens to the suspended electoral timetable.
Resignation has saved Nigeria from FIFA ban – Odegbami
Former Super Eagles captain, Segun Odegbami believes Gusau’s resignation removes the possibility of a FIFA ban and provides an opportunity for reforms.
“His resignation removes the whole issue of FIFA ban and provides the opportunity for us to clean up whatever it is that we are complaining about,” he said
Odegbami said the development could open the door for significant changes in Nigerian football.
However, former Gombe State Football Association chairman, Ahmed Shuaibu Gara-Gombe, criticised the process that led to Gusau’s departure.
“The power now goes back to the congress; the powers that have been forcing him to resign. It is a wrong approach. This move may backfire and put Nigeria in crisis. You don’t clear a system by asking all the board members to resign including the General Secretary. So, who will now inform FIFA of the latest development?
“Unless FIFA compromises their standards, they won’t accept the new board. This crisis is just about to begin. I hope the hunter does not become the hunted,” he said.
Meanwhile, before yesterday’s mass resignations, two prominent Nigerians, Dr. Danladi Bako, and Yakubu Ibn Mohammed, had backed calls by football stakeholders for Gusau’s resignation.
“In the years gone by, the NFF led by Ibrahim Gusau would have been sacked by now. The continued stay in office after a woeful first tenure makes past military regimes look messianic because during General Babangida or Abacha’s regimes, the monumental failures of the current board would not have lasted long before they get fired,” said Bako, a former Sokoto State FA chairman.
On his part, Mohammed, a former Director General of the Nigeria Television Authority (NTA) urged the NSC to “Suspend the current electoral process and set up an independent review of NFF administration and finances; ensure new, inclusive guidelines that give all real stakeholders a voice; and champion urgent reforms for the NPFL, grassroots, and women’s football.”
Tinubu orders comprehensive football reform
Meanwhile, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has directed a comprehensive reform of Nigerian football following repeated failures by national teams to qualify for major regional, continental and global competitions.
The directive was disclosed by Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy.
The president said the reform must address weaknesses in governance, administration, stakeholder representation, development pathways, domestic competitions and accountability.
“Football, Nigeria’s most popular sport and the greatest beneficiary of public support, investment and national attention, has continued to struggle basically due to structural deficits within the system,” Tinubu said.
The president directed the Chairman of the National Sports Commission to work with the NFF Secretariat and football stakeholders to ensure continuity in administration while facilitating a broad reform process.
The process, according to the president, will involve engagement with FIFA and CAF while protecting Nigeria’s obligations within the international football system.
The real challenge begins now
Ibrahim Gusau’s resignation marks the end of one chapter in Nigerian football, but it does not resolve the problems that forced the change.
The crisis was built over time through a combination of poor international results, declining youth development, financial questions, stakeholder dissatisfaction and political uncertainty.
The emergency NFF Congress now faces the biggest responsibility; deciding whether Nigerian football will simply replace its leaders or undertake the deeper reforms needed to restore confidence.
Meanwhile, the NFF has moved to ensure continuity following the resignation of the General Secretary, Dr Mohammed Sanusi, with Deputy General Secretary, Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, set to assume the role in an acting capacity.

items.title: Holiday Announced for Urs of Baba Bulleh Shah
items.summary:
The Kasur district administration has announced a local holiday on Saturday, August 29, to mark the Urs of renowned Sufi poet and saint Hazrat Baba Bulleh Shah.
The three-day Urs celebrations are currently underway in Kasur, with the event entering its second day.
Authorities have also put comprehensive security arrangements in place to ensure the safety of devotees and visitors attending the celebrations.
According to the announcement, the August 29 holiday will apply to district offices working under the Deputy Commissioner of Kasur as well as relevant district government institutions.
Baba Bulleh Shah remains one of the most celebrated Sufi poets of the subcontinent. His Urs attracts large numbers of devotees to Kasur every year.

items.content:
Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, yesterday met with Seyi Tinubu as part of the ongoing move to mobilise the youth ahead of the 2027 campaigns.
Yari said Nigeria’s youth population remains the most critical constituency for communicating the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda to Nigerians.
Speaking during the visit from Seyi Tinubu to congratulate him on his appointment and to deepen collaboration between the Campaign Council and youth-stakeholders ahead of the 2027 general elections,Yari said “Young people are not just the future of this country, they are the present. If we are going to tell the true story of what this administration has achieved, from infrastructure to the economy to security, we need the youth population.
“They understand the language of today’s Nigeria in a way that no press statement alone could. My engagement with Seyi Tinubu today was about building bridges. He has consistently demonstrated genuine commitment to youth empowerment, and that is exactly the kind of energy this campaign needs.
“We are not just asking young Nigerians to vote, we are asking them to become ambassadors of the Renewed Hope story in their communities, online and offline.”
Yari further disclosed that the Campaign Council is finalising a nationwide youth outreach framework designed to harness social media, community networks, and grassroots structures to amplify government achievements and counter misinformation.
“Every young Nigerian with a phone and a voice is a potential messenger for this administration’s impact. Our job is to equip them with the facts and the platform to tell that story authentically,” he said.
Yari thanked Seyi Tinubu for the visit and for his consistent commitment to youth empowerment, describing it as a demonstration of confidence in the Campaign Council’s mandate. He also acknowledged the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande for his continued partnership on youth engagement initiatives.
The Senator commended Seyi Tinubu for his role in fostering youth engagement within the party’s structures and expressed optimism that the collaboration would translate into stronger grassroots visibility for the administration’s programmes as the campaign season intensifies.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A US federal judge has ruled that the Department of Defense of the Trump administration acted unlawfully when it targeted AI company Anthropic after the company refused to allow some military uses of its technology.
US District Judge Rita Lin described the Pentagon’s decision to label Anthropic a supply-chain risk as “illegal and baseless.” She also said that national security cannot be used as a reason to punish companies or organisations for expressing concerns about government policy.
The ruling follows a lawsuit filed by Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot. Anthropic argued that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had exceeded his authority by taking action against the company.
Judge Finds Trump Administration Acted Unlawfully Against AI Firm Anthropic
The conflict began after Anthropic rejected certain proposed uses of its AI models by the US military. The company said its technology could not safely support weapons systems and opposed using its models for domestic surveillance.
Anthropic said these restrictions were based on concerns about safety and civil rights.
The Pentagon took a different position. Officials argued that private technology companies should not be able to place limits on military operations. The department also questioned whether Anthropic could control how the military used its technology under government contracts.
In February, the Pentagon designated Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. The US government generally uses this designation for companies linked to countries it considers security threats.
Anthropic became the first publicly known US company to receive this designation.
See Also: Anthropic Tests More Capable Model 2 Internally, But Has No Public Release Plans
Judge Says Government Went too Far
Judge Lin found that the Defense Department had acted unlawfully by ordering companies working with the military to stop doing business with Anthropic.
She said national security does not give the government unlimited power to punish companies that disagree with it.
The judge had already raised concerns about the government’s actions during an earlier stage of the case. At that time, she said the government appeared to be trying to weaken Anthropic and discourage public discussion about the military use of AI.
She described the case as potentially involving retaliation under the First Amendment, which protects freedom of speech in the United States.
The AI company also argued that the government’s actions damaged its business and violated its constitutional rights.
Anthropic Welcomes the Ruling
Anthropic welcomed the latest decision and said it remains interested in working with the US government on national security applications of AI.
A company spokesperson said Anthropic wants to work with the government to use AI in ways that can benefit Americans while addressing security concerns.
The ruling could have wider implications for the growing relationship between AI companies and the US military. As governments increasingly look to advanced AI systems for defence and national security, technology companies are likely to face difficult decisions over how their models can be used.
The Pentagon and White House had not provided comments on the ruling at the time of the report.
The case also highlights a larger debate over whether AI developers should be able to place restrictions on military applications of their technology, particularly when those restrictions involve autonomous weapons, surveillance and other sensitive uses.

items.title: Sugar stocks rally continues: Balrampur Chini, Dhampur Sugar, Uttam Sugar Mills rally up to 4%. Two big triggers
items.summary: Shares of sugar companies, including Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar, Dalmia Bharat, Shree Renuka, and EID Parry, rallied up to 4% as sugar prices have surged over the past month. items.content: Shares of sugar companies, including Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar, Dalmia Bharat, Shree Renuka, and EID Parry, rallied up to 4% as sugar prices have surged over the past month. According to Central government data, retail sugar prices rose from Rs 48.18 per kg on July 20 to Rs 55.70 per kg on August 20. Retail sugar prices are currently quoted at around Rs 70 per kg.In today’s session, Balrampur Chini Mills gained over 2% to Rs 665 on the BSE, while Dhampur Sugar Mills gained 4% to Rs 178 per share. Uttam Sugar gained 3% to Rs 306 per share. Triveni Engineering shares rose 2% to Rs 288, while Eid Parry gained over 2% to Rs 815.What’s behind the sharp rise?1.) Festive period - India's sugar demand usually surges from August to November as the country celebrates festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi, Dussehra and Diwali, which leads to heightened demand for sweets, biscuits and other confectionery items.Also read: Sugar production hit by Red Rot disease, El Nino; govt taking measures: Pralhad JoshiLast ⁠month, the government ordered dealers to hold stocks for no more than 30 days, in a bid to bolster supplies. Yet, sugar prices have jumped 10% over the past one month to record high levels, and analysts expect them to remain high for at least the next three months. In this background, patchy rains and ⁠dry weather conditions have hit sugarcane crop output, which typically requires copious amounts of water for irrigation, further boosting prices.2.) Supply worries - A key trigger is the worsening supply outlook in Brazil, the world's largest sugar producer. The country has warned of a delay in the harvest amid adverse weather conditions. Adding to uncertainty, Brazil has suspended its bi-weekly harvest and production reports, leaving investors with limited visibility on the supply situation.The shift towards ethanol is further intensifying concerns over a potential sugar supply crunch. In June, 58% of Brazil's cane juice was diverted towards ethanol, given that it is likely to be more profitable than sugar. Brazil has also raised its mandatory ethanol blending target to 32% in July from 30% in June, significantly higher than the 25-27% mix seen just months earlier.Supply concerns are not limited to Brazil. Intense heatwaves and El Nino conditions across the EU and the UK have added to fears of tighter supplies, with sugar output from the region trimmed to 14.98 million tonnes. In Asia, Thailand, the world's third-largest sugar producer, has cut its projected output by 15.6% to 9.5 million tonnes. India, the world's second-largest sugar producer after Brazil, is also projecting lower sugar production. Authorities are physically verifying mill volumes to enforce strict hoarding limits.Global deficit estimates are also pointing towards a tighter market. Green Pool has projected a global sugar deficit of 3.3 million tonnes, while StoneX has estimated the shortfall at 1.7 million tonnes. The International Sugar Organisation has forecast a deficit of 0.26 million tonnes.Read more: No ethanol link, decline in sugarcane production and stockpiling driving up sugar price: ExpertsWith production concerns mounting across major sugar-producing regions and global benchmark prices continuing to climb, the supply outlook has emerged as the key factor driving the sharp move in sugar prices.Government’s bid to rescue the riseThe government has rejected a request from biscuit and bread makers seeking more time to liquidate the excess stock over the stock holding limit and mandated that the companies sell any excess stocks by August 31.The limit, recently cut from 30 days, requires bulk sugar users to hold no more than 15 days of their normal requirement. At a meeting with the food secretary, some of the country's largest companies warned that selling their stocks now and buying from the market later could push sugar prices sharply higher. They also raised concerns about meeting export orders if supplies tighten.If this stock comes back to the market by August 31, it can substantially suppress sugar prices, said trade officials. The move follows allegations by the Indian Sugar & Bio-energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) that bulk consumers had hoarded sugar. Consumers have rejected the charge.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
The Nigerian naira strengthened further against the United States dollar at the official foreign exchange market, reaching a five-month high of about ₦1,338.59 per dollar on Thursday, August 27, 2026.
The latest movement places the naira among the stronger-performing currencies in Nigeria’s foreign exchange market as improved dollar liquidity and rising external reserves continue to support the local currency.
For Friday, August 28, the latest available market data puts the dollar at around ₦1,341.66 per dollar, although the NFEM closing rate for the day will depend on trading activity and may differ from live indicative rates.
Recent official-market data had shown the naira at ₦1,343.59 per dollar on Wednesday, August 26, before strengthening further on Thursday. The improvement has been linked to sustained dollar liquidity and stronger external buffers.
In the parallel market, the dollar remained substantially higher than the official rate. AbokiFX-related market reports showed the greenback quoted around ₦1,400 to buy and ₦1,410 to sell on Thursday, August 27.
This means Nigerians looking to buy $1 in the parallel market would need about ₦1,410, while those selling $1 could receive around ₦1,400, depending on the dealer and location.
The gap between the official and parallel markets remains significant. Based on the latest indicative official rate of about ₦1,341.66 and a parallel-market selling rate of ₦1,410, the difference is approximately ₦68 per dollar.
The naira’s recent gains have coincided with a sharp improvement in Nigeria’s foreign-exchange reserves. It was reported that external reserves had risen to about $53.34 billion, an 18-year high, while improved dollar liquidity has helped ease pressure on the local currency.
For importers, travellers, students paying overseas tuition and businesses with dollar obligations, the exchange rate remains an important factor in determining the naira cost of foreign transactions.
However, the actual rate available to customers may differ from the NFEM benchmark or parallel-market quotation. Banks, Bureau de Change operators and other authorised dealers may apply different rates depending on the transaction, amount, location and prevailing market conditions.
Parallel-market rates are unofficial and can change several times during the day. The Central Bank of Nigeria does not recognise the parallel market as an official foreign-exchange market.
As of the morning of August 28, 2026, the dollar is therefore trading around ₦1,341.66 on the latest indicative market data, while parallel-market quotations remain around ₦1,400–₦1,410 per dollar.

James Hampson, Country Director, British Council Pakistan, says, “Over the last decade more than 25,000 women and girls have gone to university or school thanks to the Scotland Pakistan Scholarship Scheme, which is making quality education more affordable and ambitions more achievable. We are proud of our partnership with the Scottish Government which continues to create life changing opportunities for young women to access higher education.”
The scholarships are available to eligible female students pursuing bachelor’s and master’s programmes at HEC-recognised universities in Pakistan. The programme focuses on fields of study that are critical to Pakistan’s future development, including: Education, Agriculture and Food Security, Sustainable Energy, Health Sciences, Climate Change, and STEM Engineering.
STEM disciplines are eligible at both bachelor’s and master’s level.
The scholarship supports award-holders with:
Tuition fees for bachelor’s or master’s courses in eligible fields
University hostel costs, where applicable
Travel between home and university twice a year for students residing in on-campus hostels
Funds for research work to access quality labs, equipment and tools within the chosen course of study (master’s only)
For postgraduate applicants, the scholarship is available for two-year Master’s/MPhil programmes, while undergraduate applicants can apply for support towards four-year bachelor’s degrees in eligible subject areas.
Applicants must be Pakistani nationals currently residing in Pakistan, be pursuing an eligible degree at an HEC-recognised university and hold a confirmed admission offer. Minorities and persons with disabilities are highly encouraged to apply.
The deadline to submit applications is 15 September 2026.
Applications can be submitted online through the British Council. Further information on eligibility criteria, the application process and frequently asked questions are available at the following link:
https://www.britishcouncil.pk/scotland-pakistan-scholarships-young-women-and-girls

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung has officially introduced the Galaxy S26 FE, bringing a faster chipset and several new AI-powered features to its Fan Edition lineup. The phone focuses heavily on software and AI improvements, while most of its core hardware remains similar to the previous-generation Galaxy S25 FE.
The Galaxy S26 FE will run Android 17 with Samsung’s One UI 9 interface from the start. This makes it the first model in the Galaxy S26 family to launch with the new software.
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE Officially Launches With One UI 9 and Android 17 Features
Samsung has not officially highlighted the chipset used in the Galaxy S26 FE, but the phone is expected to feature the Exynos 2500. The 3nm chipset was previously used in the Galaxy Z Flip7.
This is a notable upgrade over the Galaxy S25 FE, which came with the Exynos 2400. The Exynos 2500 uses newer CPU cores and comes with a more powerful AMD RDNA 3-based GPU. Its NPU also offers significantly more computing hardware for AI-related tasks.
The new chipset should help the S26 FE handle demanding applications and Samsung’s growing collection of AI features more efficiently.
One UI 9 Brings Several AI Features
AI is one of the biggest highlights of the Galaxy S26 FE. Samsung has added several features that were previously introduced on its more expensive flagship devices.
One of them is My FanCam, which first appeared on Samsung’s latest foldable phones. The feature can automatically track a person in an existing video. It adjusts the zoom and keeps the selected person near the center of the frame.
The phone also supports Horizon Lock. This feature keeps videos level even when the phone rotates while recording. Samsung has also improved Nightography to produce brighter and clearer video in dark environments.
Photo Assist is another AI-based feature. It allows users to edit images using simple instructions. Users can ask the AI to change a background, turn a daytime scene into a nighttime image, or add and remove objects from a photo.
One UI 9 also brings improvements to Now Brief. Users can create text-based widgets using natural-language commands. For example, they can ask the feature to summarize certain information and present it in a simple card.
See Also: Samsung Exynos 2700 Shows Impressive Performance Against Snapdragon Chips
Familiar Display, Cameras and Battery
Apart from the new chipset and software, the Galaxy S26 FE shares much of its hardware with its predecessor.
The phone has a 6.7-inch OLED display with a 120Hz refresh rate, 1080p+ resolution, and a peak brightness of 1,900 nits.
Samsung has also kept the 4,900mAh battery. It supports 45W wired charging and 15W wireless charging.
The camera setup is also largely unchanged. The rear system includes a 50MP main camera, an 8MP telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom, and a 12MP ultra-wide camera. A 12MP camera handles selfies and video calls.
Samsung is promising seven years of operating system updates and security patches, matching the company’s long-term software support for other recent Galaxy devices.
Six months of Google AI Pro included
Samsung is also offering a new benefit with the Galaxy S26 FE. Buyers will receive a six-month trial of Google AI Pro, which is valued at $120 and includes 5TB of cloud storage.
This offer was previously associated mainly with Samsung’s premium foldable phones, so its arrival on the Fan Edition series gives the S26 FE an additional advantage.
Price and Availability
The Galaxy S26 FE will go on sale starting September 4 in Blueberry, Pistachio and Graphite colors. Some carriers may offer the phone earlier.
The base model comes with 128GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, while a 256GB version will also be available. The starting price is $700, which is $50 higher than the launch price of the 128GB Galaxy S25 FE.
Some markets will also receive a 512GB storage option.
Pricing and availability in other markers inclusing Pakistan is not clear yet. But we will update you when we get more information about it.
Overall, the Galaxy S26 FE is more of an evolution than a major hardware redesign. Its biggest changes come from the new Exynos 2500 chipset and the wider range of AI features included with One UI 9.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup SecVite is a mobile-first platform for managing events from start to finish, and the platform is already seeing strong traction.
Launched last October by founder Hameed Yusuf, SecVite allows users to create an event; invite and manage guests; handle RSVPs and approvals; sell tickets; collect payments, gifts and contributions; and check guests in using QR codes.
“We started with private celebrations like weddings, but the platform can also be used for birthdays, conferences and other events,” Yusuf told Disrupt Africa.
The idea for SecVite, in fact, came from planning his own wedding.
“I had hundreds of guests to manage and I was personally handling things like guest approvals and invitations. At some point I realised there had to be a better way to do it,” he said.
A senior software engineer with over 10 years of experience, Yusuf started building a solution himself, and used his wedding as the first real test.
“We managed more than 400 guests through SecVite, and over 300 guests were checked in using QR codes,” he said. “That was important because it meant we were not just building something in theory. We had actually used it in a real event with hundreds of people.”
He then formally launched SecVite, a platform he said differentiates itself by its end-to-end nature and the fact it works for different types of events.
“What stood out to me was how many different tools people use to organise one event.
You might have WhatsApp for communication, Google Forms for RSVPs, spreadsheets for guest lists, bank transfers for payments, paper lists at the entrance, and another platform if tickets are involved,” said Yusuf.
“It works, but it creates a lot of manual work and friction for the organiser. A lot of event platforms also focus mainly on public ticketed events. We wanted SecVite to work just as well for a private wedding or birthday where you may need guest approvals, invitations, contributions and controlled access.”
The self-funded startup now has over 600 users, and is thinking about raising pre-seed investment to help it grow.
“A lot of our first users came through my wedding, so they originally experienced SecVite as guests rather than organisers,” said Yusuf. “The next stage for us has been getting more people to actually use the platform to run their own events.”
SecVite has started onboarding other organisers and supporting external events as well.
“That has actually been very useful because we are learning things that you don’t always discover while building the product,” said Yusuf. “Right now, I care more about seeing organisers use SecVite repeatedly for real events than just trying to grow the user number as quickly as possible.”
SecVite is focused on weddings, birthdays, private celebrations and other events where managing guests and running the event day can quickly become stressful.
“Longer-term, we see SecVite expanding across Africa because a lot of the problems we are solving are not unique to Nigeria. But I don’t want us to rush into too many countries. The priority is getting the product and business model right in Nigeria first, then expanding from there,” Yusuf said.
Organisers can start using SecVite without paying an upfront fee, with the startup instead making money when transactions happen through an event. Depending on the transaction, SecVite charges a service fee of between five and 7.5 per cent.
“This can include ticket purchases, cash gifts and contributions, vendor payments and our digital Money Spray feature,” Yusuf said. “We are still very early, so we don’t have meaningful revenue or profit yet. At this stage, We are more focused on proving that organisers will keep using SecVite and that guests will actually transact through the platform. Once we prove that consistently, the revenue side becomes much easier to scale.”
